Terms of Service

Last Updated: September 21, 2026

These Terms of Service (“Terms”) govern your access to and use of Verity’s website, platform, services, and any associated reimbursement, billing, or document workflows. By creating an account, using our service, submitting documents, or initiating a reimbursement or subscription, you agree to these Terms and our Privacy Policy.

1. Scope of the Service

Verity is a document organization and financial-record management platform. It supports users in creating, organizing, and reviewing records, and it includes workflows for reimbursement package creation, external verification, and subscription billing.

  • Service purpose: Verity is designed to help users organize records and manage payment-related workflows in a structured way.
  • Not a guarantor or arbiter: Verity does not determine whether a payment is owed, whether a reimbursement is valid, or whether a third party has a valid claim against another party.
  • No responsibility for third-party disputes: Verity is not a mediator, payment guarantor, insurer, or dispute-resolution service for disagreements between two parties, individuals, or businesses.

2. Account Eligibility and Security

To access the platform, you must provide accurate information and maintain secure control of your account.

  • Account responsibility: You are responsible for all activity that occurs under your account, including activity from any device, browser, or authenticated session associated with your account.
  • Verification requirements: We may require email verification, identity checks, Turnstile verification, or other controls to prevent fraud and abuse.
  • Single user use: Accounts are intended for individual use. You must not share, transfer, or sell access to your account or login session.
  • No impersonation: You may not create an account, submit a reimbursement request, or use the service under false, misleading, or impersonated identity.

3. Reimbursements, Third-Party Payments, and Disputes

Reimbursement workflows in Verity are user-generated and user-controlled. A reimbursement package is simply a structured request and payment flow created within the platform; it does not by itself establish that a payment is valid, due, or approved.

The current codebase does not enforce a business-only restriction on reimbursement package creation. Any authenticated user may create a package and send it to a recipient email or registered contact. Verity does not validate the underlying business relationship, legal entitlement, or commercial status of the parties.

  • No approval guarantee: Creating or sending a reimbursement package does not mean Verity has verified the underlying obligation, invoice, receipt, or business relationship.
  • Third-party disputes: Verity takes no responsibility for disputes between the party creating the reimbursement request, the recipient, the payer, or any third party. Any disagreement about whether a payment is valid, required, or owed must be resolved between those parties.
  • Stripe onboarding and business verification: To receive payouts, the package creator (the intended payee) must complete Stripe Connect onboarding and have an active payout account (the code enforces this via the creator's StripeAccount.is_active check). Stripe may require business or identity verification during onboarding.
  • Recipient verification: Recipients should verify the identity of the sender, the requested amount, the records attached, and the business purpose before paying or accepting a reimbursement request.
  • Independent review required: Users should review receipts, invoices, contracts, policies, and any supporting records before sending or paying anything. Verity encourages users to confirm details independently before proceeding.
  • Fraud and misrepresentation: Any attempt to submit fabricated, duplicate, or misleading reimbursement records is prohibited. The product may detect and block suspicious activity, but it does not guarantee the underlying transaction is legitimate.

4. Abuse Prevention and Security Controls

To protect the platform, other users, and the integrity of reimbursement and billing flows, Verity implements technical and review-based controls. We may intervene when we detect suspicious, fraudulent, or abusive activity.

  • Rate limits and verification gates: We may limit repeated attempts, enforce challenge checks, and require additional confirmation when abnormal traffic, account abuse, or bot behavior is detected.
  • Bot and automation restrictions: Use of automated scripts, bots, scraping tools, credential stuffing, spam, or bulk generation of requests is prohibited.
  • Manual review: Suspect activity may be delayed pending manual review. In such cases, we may request more information, suspend service temporarily, or permanently restrict the account.
  • Enforcement actions: We may warn, throttle, suspend, ban, deny a reimbursement, cancel a subscription, reverse a payment, or report abuse as warranted by the circumstances and applicable law.

5. Billing, Subscriptions, and Paid Features

Some services are offered on a paid basis. Billing may be processed through Stripe or other payment providers.

  • Subscription terms: Paid plans may be monthly or otherwise recurring. By subscribing, you agree to the recurring charges associated with the selected plan.
  • Plan changes and renewals: Subscription upgrades, downgrades, and renewals are subject to the pricing and timing disclosed for the selected plan at checkout.
  • No duplicate checkout intent: Repeated or accidental duplicate purchase attempts may be rejected or reconciled to avoid duplicate subscriptions or repeated charges.
  • Cancellation: You may cancel in accordance with the plan terms and applicable payment provider settings. Cancellation generally prevents future renewals but does not automatically reverse already processed charges.
  • Refunds: Refund eligibility is determined by the applicable plan and our billing policy. We may refuse refunds for fraudulent, abusive, or policy-violating use.
  • Payment disputes: Chargebacks, payment disputes, or unauthorized billing complaints may trigger account review and restrictions. Verity does not assume responsibility for disputes that are fundamentally between a payer and a counterparty.
